title: Knowledge check: Color Contrast and Visual Accessibility

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly covered by “Color Contrast and Visual Accessibility” in the source syllabus?
options: Relationship between HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
questions.explanation: The syllabus lists “Text and background contrast” under “Color Contrast and Visual Accessibility”. Apply this topic in the lesson example and confirm its actual browser behavior.

questions.prompt: When applying color contrast and visual accessibility in a real interface, which approach is the strongest default?
options: Use color alone to communicate meaning and skip text labels.
Assume a visible style automatically provides application behavior.
Load multiple Bootstrap JavaScript builds to ensure each control works.
Use the documented pattern, preserve semantic HTML, and test the relevant state.
questions.answer_key: Use the documented pattern, preserve semantic HTML, and test the relevant state.
questions.explanation: Prefer documented conventions and semantic markup. Verify responsive and interaction behavior, accessibility, and runtime assumptions instead of relying on appearance alone.

questions.prompt: Which verification step best complements a lesson on color contrast and visual accessibility?
options: Trust the CSS class name without checking the loaded Bootstrap version.
Record the expected result, reproduce the relevant state, and test the change at a second viewport or interaction state.
Publish the result after checking only the default viewport.
Remove all labels and focus indicators to reduce visual clutter.
questions.answer_key: Trust the CSS class name without checking the loaded Bootstrap version.
questions.explanation: A repeatable check compares expected and actual behavior and includes a relevant viewport or interaction state. Document what was checked and what still needs review.
